marc:datafield.marc:subfield: 牧野诡事 | Mu ye gui shi

he book contains four chapters—Searching for Dragons in the Tomb, Worlds Within the Mirror, Ancient Capital in the Clouds, and Thus I Heard—each featuring strange and mysterious tales drawn from folklore, legends, and the author’s personal experiences. The structure resembles that of traditional Chinese zhiguai (records of the strange) fiction, while the writing style bears a strong resemblance to Tianxia Bachang’s signature narrative voice. With a street-level perspective narrating grand and fantastical adventures, the stories are full of dramatic twists and gripping suspense. Among the memorable legends are tales such as Lord Horse’s Mountain-Gazing Grave Site, The Zombie Village beneath Fuxian Lake, Fire Beetles, The Wrathful Chicken, and The Corpse-Driving Men of Western Hunan. Many of these stories later inspired iconic IP works by Tianxia Bachang himself
